privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This notice explains what information Wave uses to operate the marketplace and how you can contact us about it.

sections.heading: Who controls your data
paragraphs: The data controller is UD SteelCode, Školska 10, 72000 Zenica, Bosnia and Herzegovina. For privacy questions, contact info{'@'}wave.ba.

sections.heading: Information we handle
paragraphs: Depending on how you use Wave, this can include account and contact details, creator or company profile information, campaigns, applications, messages, self-reported social metrics, and technical or security logs.

sections.heading: Purposes and legal bases
paragraphs: Account registration, profiles, applications, offers, messages and requested support are processed to provide the service and perform our agreement with you. Required account details are necessary to create and secure an account; optional profile fields can be left blank.

Security, abuse prevention, moderation and limited profile-setup tips serve our legitimate interests in a safe, usable marketplace. Tips contain account setup guidance, stop after at most four messages or profile completion, and can be disabled. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests.

Newsletter, campaign alerts, analytics and advertising use separate opt-ins. You may withdraw consent at any time without affecting earlier lawful processing. We also process data where required by law, for example responding to a valid authority request. We do not make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects solely by automated processing.

sections.heading: Public information
paragraphs: Profile and campaign details submitted for public display can be viewed by other users and visitors. Do not include private or sensitive information in public fields.

sections.heading: Data exchanged between users
paragraphs: Each user processes personal data received from other users, such as names, contact details, delivery addresses, photos or videos, as an independent controller and is responsible for it under applicable law. Wave only transmits and stores this data to operate the platform.

Use the data you receive only for the agreed collaboration, do not pass it to third parties without a legal basis, and delete it when it is no longer needed. Wave is not responsible for its processing outside the platform.

sections.heading: Providers and international processing
paragraphs: Hetzner Online GmbH hosts Wave’s database, files and recovery backups in Germany. Brevo (Brevo SAS, France) delivers emails using recipients’ addresses, names and message contents; its published database hosting locations are France, Germany and Belgium.

Cloudflare, Inc. provides proxy/CDN and security services. It processes network request data, including IP addresses, URLs and browser information, and may cache public resources. Its global network can process data outside Bosnia and Herzegovina and the EEA. Optional Google, Apple and Meta services may also involve international processing.

International transfers require a basis and safeguards under applicable law, which may include recognized adequacy decisions or contractual safeguards. Contact us for information about the applicable arrangements and how to obtain a copy. A provider’s EU headquarters alone does not mean all processing stays in the EU. We do not sell personal data.

sections.heading: Retention and deletion
paragraphs: Account and profile data are retained while the account is active. Deleting an account removes personal profile fields, owned files, subscriptions and access tokens from the live application. Shared messages and collaboration records can remain for other participants with account identifiers anonymized; message text you previously wrote is not automatically rewritten. Do not send unnecessary sensitive information.

Recovery backups rotate within 14 days of creation. Deleted data can remain in an older backup until it expires; backups are used for recovery rather than active account access. Application logs and encrypted email previews have a 14-day cleanup period. Completed or discarded queue jobs are removed after 30 days.

Brevo keeps its own email delivery records separately; Wave’s 14-day local-log rule does not set Brevo’s retention. Contact us about removal of provider-held records. Support, moderation, consent and shared collaboration records are retained only as necessary to resolve the matter, serve participants, meet legal obligations or establish/defend claims; necessity is assessed when a case closes and on deletion requests.

Withdrawing a newsletter subscription stops that subscription, while a minimal withdrawal record may be retained to respect your choice and demonstrate it. Existing subscriptions without recorded opt-in are not evidence of explicit consent.

sections.heading: Your choices and requests
paragraphs: Where applicable, you may request access to, correction or deletion of your personal information, or ask about restriction, portability, or objection rights. Contact info{'@'}wave.ba. We may need to verify your request before acting.

If you believe that the processing of your personal data does not comply with applicable law, you can lodge a complaint with the Personal Data Protection Agency in Bosnia and Herzegovina or another competent supervisory authority.

Send rights requests to info{'@'}wave.ba. We respond without undue delay, normally within 30 days; any lawful extension and its reasons will be explained. We request only proportionate information needed to verify identity. Accounts are for adults aged 18 or older.

If you choose Google or Apple sign-in, the selected provider processes authentication information under its own privacy terms.

With separate Marketing consent, Meta Pixel may process technical browser, URL and registration data to measure advertising. Meta processes that data under its privacy policy. You can withdraw consent using Cookie preferences.

sections.heading: Email and your choices
paragraphs: Email verification, security notices and service messages about your account and collaborations are part of operating Wave and do not depend on a newsletter subscription.

Profile completion tips are enabled for new accounts. The series contains up to four reminders and stops when your profile is complete. You can turn them off in email settings or through the unsubscribe link in the message.

You receive Wave news (the newsletter) only if you opt in. Newsletter and profile tips have separate email settings. Subscribing is not required to create or use an account; you can unsubscribe in email settings or in the message itself.

sections.heading: Messages, links and notifications
paragraphs: Conversations are not public. Messages, replies and reactions are shown to conversation participants. To display a link preview, Wave may fetch public metadata and an image from the linked website.
You enable push notifications by granting permission on your device. Wave stores the subscription details needed for delivery; you can disable notifications in your account or device settings.

You can delete your account in settings. Personal data and owned files are removed under the deletion policy; shared collaboration and message history may remain available to other participants with your account anonymized.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: Wave uses essential storage for core features. Google Analytics and Meta Pixel are optional and load only with separate analytics or marketing consent.

sections.heading: Essential session cookie
paragraphs: When a secure account session is needed, Wave uses a first-party session cookie to keep you signed in and protect account actions. It is marked HttpOnly and uses the browser's same-site protections. It is not used for advertising.

sections.heading: Local browser storage
paragraphs: Wave stores your chosen language and cookie preferences in local browser storage. These values are not cookies and are not used to track you across other websites.

sections.heading: Progressive web app
paragraphs: If you install Wave or use a browser with service-worker support, the app may cache static interface files so it can load reliably. The service worker precaches app assets and does not cache private API responses.

sections.heading: Manage browser data
paragraphs: Change or withdraw analytics or marketing consent using Cookie preferences in the footer. Your choice is saved in your browser. Clearing site data may sign you out and show this notice again.

sections.heading: Cookie and storage list
paragraphs: PHPSESSID (cookie, Wave): signing in and protecting account actions. Necessary; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax; lasts up to 90 days.
wave-locale (local storage, Wave): your chosen language. Necessary; kept until you clear it.
wave-cookie-consent-v3 (local storage, Wave): your analytics and marketing choices, the policy version and the time. Necessary; valid for 180 days, then we ask again.
wave.registration-intent (local storage, Wave): the page you return to after registering. Necessary; removed after use or after 14 days.
Service worker cache (Wave): app files for faster loading. Necessary; replaced with every update.
_ga and _ga_… (cookies, Google Analytics): measuring visits. Only with analytics consent; last up to 180 days.
_fbp and _fbc (cookies, Meta Pixel): measuring ads. Only with marketing consent; Meta sets their lifetime, and Wave deletes them when you withdraw consent.

Cloudflare may set necessary security cookies such as __cf_bm (normally 30 minutes) or cf_clearance (according to the configured challenge duration), if those security features are active. They are used for bot/challenge protection, independently of optional analytics or marketing.

sections.heading: Analytics cookies
paragraphs: If a Google Analytics measurement ID is configured, Wave loads Google Analytics only after you enable Analytics. It may then use first-party analytics cookies to measure visits and site usage. If you choose Only necessary, the Analytics tag is not loaded.
You can withdraw consent later from Cookie preferences. Wave then stops sending analytics events and removes Google Analytics cookies set on this site.

sections.heading: Marketing cookies (Meta Pixel)
paragraphs: When configured and Marketing is allowed, Meta Pixel measures public-page visits and successful registrations to assess Facebook and Instagram ads. It may use _fbp and _fbc cookies. Meta may receive technical information including your IP address, browser information, URL and referring page.

Wave adds only the account category, known company type and registration method to registration events. We do not add names, email addresses, phone numbers, messages or negotiated amounts to marketing events. Automatic advanced matching is disabled.
Withdraw consent using Cookie preferences. Wave then stops its marketing events and deletes Meta cookies it can remove on this domain. Registration and all core features work without marketing.

Whoever sends content confirms that they hold the necessary rights and consents, including the consent of every person who can be seen or heard in it and, for minors, the consent of a parent or guardian.

Do not send malicious files or links. Wave does not guarantee that other users’ files and links are safe, so open them with care. Keep copies of your work outside Wave; Wave is not a long-term storage service.

Users resolve disputes about delivery, quality, payment or rights between themselves. Wave may help through reports and moderation but is not a mediator or arbitrator. sections.heading: Voluntary collaborations

sections.heading: Platform charges and credits

Before introducing paid features, we will publish prices, credit rules, taxes, termination and applicable consumer rights. A charge requires a clear prior offer and your acceptance; these terms do not authorize future charges.

sections.heading: Your content and rights

You give Wave a non-exclusive permission to store, technically process and display content according to your visibility choices, including thumbnails and share cards. Permission lasts as needed for display and permitted shared history. Using content in a separate Wave advertisement requires separate permission.

sections.heading: Advertising and conduct

sections.heading: Reviews, reports and moderation

find-creators.title: How to find an influencer for a collaboration
find-creators.intro: From your campaign goal to a shortlist of creators who fit your brand.

sections.heading: Start with your goal and audience
sections.body: Write down who you want to reach and what you want to achieve: introduce a product, explain a service or share an experience. Choose the country and platform where that audience is active.

sections.heading: Review the content, not just the numbers
sections.body: Filter the directory by country, category and platform. Open profiles and portfolios. Consider each creator’s style, topics and approach to presenting brands.

sections.heading: Propose a concrete next step
sections.body: Send a package inquiry with a description of your task, or create a campaign with clear requirements. Compare relevant responses and discuss the details before starting the collaboration.

choose-package.title: How to choose a creator package
choose-package.intro: Compare content, scope and prices before sending a collaboration inquiry.

sections.heading: Check what the package includes
sections.body: Review the platform, number of posts, format and package description. Distinguish content posted on a creator’s channel from UGC a brand plans to use on its own channels.

sections.heading: Compare scope and price
sections.body: Creators set the prices shown on their profiles. Ask about filming, editing, revisions, deadlines and content usage. Compare offers with the same scope rather than assuming an average market price.

sections.heading: Send a detailed inquiry
sections.body: Include the product, content you need, deadline and available budget. Once the creator accepts the inquiry, continue the conversation and confirm the agreed scope before production.

campaign-brief.title: How to write a campaign brief
campaign-brief.intro: A clear brief helps creators understand the task, deadlines and budget.

sections.heading: Explain the idea and deliverables
sections.body: Write a short summary, introduce the product and describe the audience. Choose Instagram, TikTok or YouTube and specify the format and number of deliverables.

sections.heading: Include budget, timing and creator count
sections.body: Enter a budget range, location, application deadline and the number of creators you need. Explain content delivery timing and required materials in the campaign description.

sections.heading: Leave room for creativity
sections.body: Separate essential information from suggestions. Review applicants’ profiles, invite suitable creators to a conversation and agree on the final plan.

creatorGuides.title: Guides for creators
creatorGuides.intro: Build your profile, present your services and find campaigns that fit your work.

create-profile.title: How to build your creator profile
create-profile.intro: Show what you do and help brands understand why they should work with you.

sections.heading: Introduce your work
sections.body: Add a profile photo, a short bio, your city and areas of interest in your account. Choose the creator types that describe your work, such as influencer, UGC creator, photographer or videographer. Creator types describe your services; platforms are the channels where you publish.

sections.heading: Add channels and portfolio
sections.body: Link your social profiles and enter accurate audience figures. Add portfolio examples that show your style: photographs, videos or previous collaborations. A few relevant pieces with context help brands assess your work better than a large, unstructured collection.

sections.heading: Review your public profile
sections.body: Check your public profile preview, including the photo, bio, portfolio and packages. Add frequently asked questions so brands know what to expect. Confirm your email and follow your account approval status. Hiding your account makes your profile unavailable to other users.

offer-packages.title: How to present your services
offer-packages.intro: Create clear packages brands can understand and compare before sending an inquiry.

sections.heading: Define content and scope
sections.body: In your collaboration packages, describe what you create, for which platform and in what quantity. A package might include one short video or a set of photographs. Distinguish content production from publication on your own channel and explain what the price includes.

sections.heading: Set pricing and terms
sections.body: State your price, delivery timeframe and included revisions. Specify when usage rights, additional versions or travel costs require a separate agreement. For work without a fixed scope, offer a custom inquiry and ask for a concrete brief.

sections.heading: Respond to collaboration inquiries
sections.body: When a company requests your package, review its message and expectations before accepting. After acceptance, discuss details in the conversation. Decline if the project does not fit your work or availability; the company will be notified.

apply-to-campaigns.title: How to apply to a campaign
apply-to-campaigns.intro: Find a relevant brief and send an application that shows how you can help the brand.

sections.heading: Choose the right campaign
sections.body: Check the campaign category, platforms, deliverables, budget and application deadline. Review the location and number of creators needed. Apply when you can deliver the work and the brand fits your audience or creative style.

sections.heading: Send a specific application
sections.body: Explain why you fit the campaign and propose a short content idea. Highlight relevant portfolio work and confirm your availability.

sections.heading: Follow the response and agree on details
sections.body: Track applications in your account. A company can also invite you directly without a prior application; you can accept or decline. After acceptance, agree on the brief, deadlines and delivery in the conversation. Applying does not automatically mean you have been hired.
